# Registries (the extension points)

gelpy has no if/elif dispatch on model names. Each pluggable family is a registry: a new
entry is a subclass plus a decorator, and it becomes selectable from the CLI immediately.
See [extending](../guide/extending.md) for what each one requires of a new entry.

`gelpy models list --kind fit|shape|background` prints names, descriptions and parameter
schemas at the terminal.

## Fit strategies

Selected with `fit run --method`. Registry: `gelpy.core.peaks.strategies.fit_strategy_registry`.

| name | description |
|---|---|
| `bayesian` | Seeded posterior sampling around the MAP (Tier 3). |
| `grow_select` | Residual-driven grow-and-select (default). |
| `sparse_seed` | Non-negative-deconvolution seeding (Tier 2). |

## Peak shapes

Selected with `fit run --shapes`. Registry: `gelpy.core.peaks.peak_registry`.

| name | description |
|---|---|
| `bi_gaussian` | Split Gaussian with independent left/right widths. |
| `emg` | Exponentially-modified Gaussian (right-tailed) peak. |
| `gaussian` | Symmetric Gaussian peak. |
| `pseudo_voigt` | Gaussian/Lorentzian blend (sharp, heavy wings). |

## Background models

Selected with `background remove --model`. Registry: `gelpy.core.background.background_registry`.

| name | description |
|---|---|
| `plane_ransac` | RANSAC-fit 2D plane through two background stripes, then subtract it. |
| `robust_plane` | Iterative-reweighted least-squares fit of a low-order background surface; no stripes needed, robust to bands/smears via the signal-is-positive asymmetry. |


Parameter schemas:

`plane_ransac`:

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stripes` | `any` | `None` | (start_row, height) background stripes; None = heuristic default. |

`robust_plane`:

| parameter | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `integer` | `1` | Polynomial surface order: 0=offset, 1=plane (default), 2=quadratic (captures vignetting/curvature; opt-in — can bend into diffuse haze). |
| `weight_mode` | `string` | `'probabilistic'` | 'probabilistic' (default): two-component mixture, σ self-scaled to the noise floor — robust when signal covers a large image fraction. 'asymmetric': fixed Eilers ALS weight (simpler, no σ estimation). |
| `asymmetry_p` | `number` | `0.02` | Weight given to above-surface (signal) pixels in 'asymmetric' mode. |
| `signal_prior` | `number` | `0.3` | Prior fraction of signal pixels for the 'probabilistic' mixture. |
| `max_iter` | `integer` | `15` | Max IRLS iterations. |
| `tol` | `number` | `0.001` | Convergence tol on max weight change between iterations. |
| `subsample` | `integer` | `1` | Fit the surface on every n-th pixel (lossless for a smooth surface); it is evaluated on the full grid without full-resolution coordinate grids. Speed and memory escape hatch for very large images. |
| `contiguity` | `number` | `0.0` | Spatial-smoothing sigma (px) applied to the weight field each iteration; 0 disables. Makes weights coherent so isolated hot pixels aren't trusted as background. |
| `clip_negative` | `boolean` | `False` | If True, clamp negatives to 0 (legacy behaviour). Default False keeps signed residuals so the baseline stays centered at 0 — clamping rectifies noise into a positive pedestal that biases downstream peak integrals. |

## Lane projection strategies

Selected with `lanes detect --projection-strategy`. Registry: `gelpy.core.lanes.projection_strategies`.

| name | description |
|---|---|
| `d4_union` | Multi-band union — cluster rows into candidate y-bands by comb-periodicity, greedily keep the bands that add all-N lane coverage, and project over their union. Targets gels where different lanes carry bands at different y (e.g. ladder/scaffold vs samples), where no single y-window covers every lane. |
| `full` | Full-height column mean — the baseline every strategy must beat. |
